Cath Lab is working

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After almost two years of delays and broken promises at the cost of human life, the Catheterization Lab at PE provincial hospital is finally working

Summary:
According to the head of paediatric cardiology at PE provincial hospital babies with congenital heart disease have been dying because the Catheterisation laboratory needed to save their lives has been out of service. After two years and many broken promises the Cath Lab is finally fully operation, we get a tour of the site

Further information:
We recap what has transpired over the past two years - what we have reported
Hear from previous parents distress- Elmarie and lulu

But now the Lab is finally operational - Taken into the lab and see a Cath being done - I hoping this is Zenanda - I planted the seed. Just said we would like to see where the children we have spoken to in the past are now.
How will they catch up with regards to the waiting list
How many kids will be done a week
And how are these Cath's then going to translate into surgeries? - Still no contracted surgeon or anaesthetist in EC

Elmarie - her fight is finally over!
Lulu Sifuba - her daughter Zenanda can now get treatment

Conclusion: we will be watching closely to see if the department delivers are what they have promised here today


Expert:
Mr. Siyanda Manana

Script:


A Catheterization Laboratory is a basic tool for a cardiologist today and is used to diagnose heart disease. It’s also used for non-invasive surgical Procedures, which is an AN ESSENTIAL lifesaving service for babies born with congenital heart disease.
In 2018 the only Catherization Laboratory in the Eastern Cape, at the time, Stopped working. Leaving some 6 million patients lives in danger

DR Pepeta – babies will die

When we first reported on the story in march 2019 The previous head of Cardiology Dr Pepeta was clear that babies were dying, while the department of health failed to get the Cath Lab up and running. We spoke to moms like Elmarie van zyl whose children were hanging onto life while they were ignored and left out in the cold by the department of health

ELMARIE: As a heart mom you are always going, then you don’t sleep, you listen to the breathing you make sure they are okay, you check the stats.


At the time the HOD Dr thobile MBengashe Promised us that the equipment had been ordered and the lab was on track to been in stalled

2019: HOD: 29th of mARCH ITS LANDING AND WE NEED 9 WEEKS TO PUT IN IT. tAKE THE old one out and put the new one in. The Cath is going to be in place in 9 weeks

9 weeks later the lab was not operational as promised. In July 2019 we returned to find that the equipment had arrived, but it was now sitting outside the hospital in shipping containers
Again the department was adamant that they would have the lab fully operation in a few months

2019: Rolene: Our predicated completion date and handover to us is the 9th September

Almost a year later we returned again to find out why the Cath lab was still not working and the Department of health blatantly ignored our requested for an interview they also refused us access on the premises.

Upsound mac.

We did manage to speak to the current head of cardiology who said exactly what Dr pepete had said two years before. Children were dying, due to the Depoartment of healths failure to get the NEW Cath Lba at PE pROVINCIAL HOSPITAL INSTALLED AND WAOKRING

Andile

When we first met Lulu Sifuba she had been fighting for two years to get treatment for her daughter Zenanda, she had all but given up.



Lulu – they keep postponing
She will die

After being informed that the Cath Lab was fully installed and operational, We returned to PE this past week to see it for ourselves. And finally after two years of broken promise and missed deadlines, we can report that the Cath Lab at PE provincial hospital is working.


Andile
How many Caths

After years of anxiously waiting, Lulu’s daughter Zenanda is scheduled to get her Caths done on the 9th of November

Lulu – upsound
Andile – prep for surgery and so happy

In a few weeks time Joshua will be having his finally life saving surgery at Nelson Mandela children’s hospital in Johannesburg

I can breath


Although the lab in now up and running, the next big challenge is to try and get all the pediatric patients on the long waiting list treated as soon as possible

Saving lives
